clusters.name: space inside a number ('2 0 ft', '1 4 ft', '5 00 kips', 'KL/r = 15 0')
clusters.guess: This is the largest source of wrong answers: 27 of 60 pure copies are DIFFERENT. The reader keeps only one digit group of a number split by a space and calculates with it. '2 0 ft' gives KL = 0 ft and phi Pn = 1190; '1 4 ft' gives KL = 3.2; '5 00 kips' gives Pu = 5 kips and a W10X12; '15 0' gives phi Fcr = 44.3; '1 8 k live' gives Mu = 99.2. Even a length of 0 ft is accepted. Suggested fix (a new file or reader.js): when two digit groups are separated only by a space, stop and ask which number was meant. Exceptions are a shape such as 'w12 53', a mixed number '1 1/8', and an 'a x b' size. Never calculate with a length or load of 0.

clusters.name: '?' typed in the middle of a sentence splits the question
clusters.guess: A '?' inside a clause is read as the end of a question. The text is cut into parts, each part loses the other's data, and a missing D or L is calculated as 0. '25 kips dead? and 5 kips live' gives U = 8 kips. '85 kips ... and? an occupancy live load of 95' gives two answers, 119 and 152. 'fixed at both? ends' answers the Euler question with phi Pn = 298. 'Find? the effective net area Ae' loses the asked Ae and prints phi Pn = 205.5 instead. Suggested fix: split at '?' only when what follows starts a new question. A missing D or L must stay MISSING, never 0. When the asked quantity is lost, the form's default answer must not be printed.

clusters.name: two problems lettered by himself, merged ('a. .. b. ..', 'a .. b ..', sometimes 'a) .. b) ..')

findings.cluster: space inside a number ('2 0 ft', '1 4 ft', '5 00 kips', 'KL/r = 15 0')
findings.which_is_right: clean. He keeps every digit (HOW-HE-TYPES lists '2 0 ft' as a space inside ONE number), so the paper's number is the joined one. Examples: BC-037 KL = 20 ft gives phi Pn = 877 kips (Table 4-1a), not 1190. BC-025 Pu = 500 gives W10X49, not W10X12. BL-050 KL/r = 150 gives phi Fcr = 10 ksi, not 44.3. BC-076 Mu = 163.2, not 99.2. BC-107 is 254 kips, not 119. A second group of only zeros ('2 0', '5 00', '40 0', '15 0', '1 00') can only be one number. A second group like '1 4', '2 5' or '8 5' could also be a count and a value ('2 5-kip loads'). Those have two readings, so the page must STOP rather than join them.
findings.root_cause: ext/reader.js:138 scanQuantities reads numbers as space-separated tokens. The group next to the unit is taken ('2 0 ft' -> 0 ft, '1 4 ft' -> 4 ft). After '=' the readers bind the first group ('Pu = 5 00 kips' -> 5, 'KL/r = 15 0' -> 15, 'Mu = 32 0' -> 32). The other group has no unit, and both safety nets skip unitless numbers: reader.js:2612 ('if (!q.unit ...) return;' in the unplaced list) and pipeline.js:2365 extraCandidates / 2438 computeUnused, which only check stresses and counts. So the lost group is dropped silently, and even KL = 0 ft is calculated (BC-037: phi Pn = 1190). Nothing before the readers (normalizeTyped pipeline.js:1821, repairSpelling) looks at digit-space-digit.

findings.root_cause: Every splitter cuts at '?' with no condition. The frozen finder's sentences() (finder.js:44) uses ([?;:])\s+. pipeline.js sentenceList (594) copies it. looksLikeAsk (593) counts any segment holding '?' as an ask. splitAsks (646) then makes each '?' segment its own part, and a part's stem is ONLY the non-ask segments. So the data inside the segment before the '?' ('25 kips dead?') is not seen by the other part. The loads forms calculate an empty D or L as 0, which gives U = 8 kips and the two answers 119 and 152. For 'Find? the effective net area Ae', the ask segment is just 'Find?', so askedInWords sees no Ae and the form's default phi Pn line is printed as ANSWER. For 'fixed at both? ends', the finder's question sentence becomes the '... both?' clause and routes to column capacity. normalizeTyped (pipeline.js:1862) handles only '= ?'.

What is the governing factored load?"  -> baseline: part 1 refused, part 2 ANSWER U = 8 kips (right: 38). Also "Find? the effective net area Ae of an L6 x 6 x 1/2 angle connected through one leg with a single line of five 7/8-in. bolts." -> baseline ANSWER phi Pn = 205.5 (right: ANSWER TO Ae = 4.22 in^2).
findings.fix_proposal: SOLVE_TYPED.strayMarks(t), in the same new file, called with one line in normalizeTyped right after the '= ?' -> blank rule (pipeline.js:1862). Because it runs before the frozen finder, every splitter sees the repaired text. Only a '?' glued to a word and followed by a word is considered. It is taken OUT when the word before it cannot end a question (find, what, is, of, for, and, the, a, both, ...), or when its clause (from the last . ? ! ; : or newline) does not start with a question or instruction word ('The service loads ... dead?', 'a simply supported floor?'). It STAYS when the next thing is a part letter ('? b)', '? b The'), a number, a blank or a unit ('is? kips' may be a blank), a Capitalised word ('True or false? Loads'), the end of the text, or when its clause starts as a question ('what is Pu? the column ...'). Must NOT break 'Vu = ?' blanks, true/false headers, or real question ends before a new problem. Separate guard to file for unit A: a loads_* form must never calculate a D or L that the words mention with 0 (21 probes still do, e.g. A2-loads-p32 'D = L = 20 k' -> 32 kips; A1-tsel-09 'live load 3 times the dead load' -> 1.4D).
